paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub Awesome. Today we're checking out 28 self-hosted projects you can run on your own hardware. Let's get into it.

Kanzo is a kanban board that runs in your browser and doubles as an MCP server. So you and your coding agents share the same task list. Run one command and the board opens on your machine. Your agents connect to it, move cards between columns, and leave comments as they work while you watch and steer. The whole board lives in one folder and syncs between computers through a private git repo you own.

Traccar is an open-source GPS tracking platform you can run yourself. It speaks more than 200 GPS protocols and works with over 2,000 tracker models, so almost any device can report in. Locations land in your own SQL database, and you follow everything live on a web dashboard or a phone app. You can draw geofences that alert you when a vehicle enters or leaves an area and pull reports on trips and driver behavior.

Suna is a self-hostable platform for running AI agents that do real work for a team, built on OpenCode agents. Each agent works in its own isolated cloud sandbox on its own git branch. You can hand them tasks from Slack or Microsoft Teams or set them off on a schedule or a webhook. They plug into thousands of apps through connectors and MCP, and every tool can be set to allow, ask, or block.

Dossier is a self-hosted job search app that writes resumes and cover letters tailored to each, built with Next.js and PostgreSQL. You keep one career profile with all your real experience. Paste in a job posting or search job boards and the AI pulls out what the employer wants and shows how well you match. Then it drafts your documents from your profile. You polish them in a chat and export them as PDFs.

Doska is an open-source kanban board with a built-in markdown editor made with React and Tauri and running on the web, Mac, Windows, and Linux. Everything saves on your device first, so it's fast and works offline. Then it syncs either to a plain folder where boards become folders and cards become markdown files or to a server for teams with live updates and shared boards.

Mitra is a self-hosted calendar and task manager that puts your events and your tasks on one timeline so you can see when you actually have time to get work done. It runs in a Docker container and keeps everything in a folder you own. So backing up that folder backs up the whole app. You get week, month, year, and timeline views, plus a planning area for tasks with no date yet.

Magic is a self-hosted platform for building apps and APIs from your database. Point its API wizard at an existing schema, and it generates endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting records. You can edit the logic, build a front end in the browser, and expose endpoints as tools for AI agents through MCP. Role-based permissions decide exactly which functions each user can call.

FreeTV is a self-hosted service that turns free-to-air TV you record at home into a TidyLex library built in Node with SQLite and run in Docker. You pick shows from its TV guide and TVHeadend records them from a tuner you own. FreeTV then files each recording into a Plex-ready folder with the right name, refreshes your library, and can clean up the original afterward.

Termix puts your server connections, credentials, and management tools in one self-hosted workspace. Open SSH sessions in split-screen tabs, move files between servers, or manage Docker containers without leaving the app. Those tools come as plugins so you can choose what to run. It works in your browser and has desktop and mobile apps with shared hosts and access controls for teams.

AgentFlux is a self-hosted AI platform for building workflows and agents, run in Docker and used from your browser. You lay out a workflow on a canvas from 17 ready-made steps with branches, templates, and undo, or just describe a task and let an agent build the workflow for you. Agents can run on demand or on a schedule and they draw on a local knowledge base of your own documents.

Dashbeam is an open-source way to send files straight from one device to another with no cloud in between on desktop, Android, the command line, and the web. It's built on Iroh, a peer-to-peer networking stack, and every transfer is encrypted with each file checked against its hash. Devices find each other with a pairing code, a share ticket, or automatically on your local network.

Leaf Pro takes Overleaf's open-source community edition and adds features for teams that want to host their own LaTeX editor. You can track changes and review comments, sync projects with GitHub or GitLab, and bring in references from Zotero or Mendeley. It also has an AI assistant and sandboxed compilation. The project is independently maintained and isn't affiliated with Overleaf.

Parson is a self-hosted music app for the collection you already own with a Rust backend and a web player. Choose your music folder and start listening. It indexes your library and plays it on the web, on desktop for Windows, Mac, and Linux, or from a Docker container. Your playlists, listening history, and recommendations all stay on a machine you control.

File Browser Quantum is a self-hosted file manager you use from your browser, built as a fork of the original File Browser project. Point it at one or more folders on your server with rules for what to include or leave out, and manage everything through a clean web interface. Search updates in real time and it shows previews for office documents, videos, and even 3D models.

Alma Relay is a relay you can host yourself so the Alma app on your phone can control Alma on your desktop from anywhere. It runs on Node or on Cloudflare Workers with Durable Objects, with a Docker setup that handles HTTPS for you. Your desktop opens a connection out to the relay and your phone's requests flow back through it, including streaming and WebSockets.

Gofer is a self-hosted email client that keeps your mail on your own machine, built in Go with HTMX and Tailwind. It handles several accounts at once and connects straight to each provider using IMAP for most, the Gmail API for Gmail, and Microsoft Graph for Outlook. Your messages are cached locally in SQLite with threads, drafts, scheduled sending, and search filters.

Contrack brings your scattered contacts into a self-hosted address book and helps you remember the conversations behind the names. Import contacts from different services, merge duplicates, and add notes or reminders for your next catchup. Connect your calendar or inbox to see meetings and conversations on each person's timeline. You can also search your notes in plain language or connect an AI assistant through MCP.

Mailflare gives your team custom domain email, calendars, file storage, and booking pages in one app you can host yourself. Create personal or shared mailboxes, set rules for incoming messages, and let people book time on your calendar. You can run it on Cloudflare or in Docker with services like Resend or Amazon SES handling email delivery. It also has AI agents for searching mail and drafting replies.

GaiaCP is an open-source billing and provisioning system for small web hosting businesses built on Laravel and Filament. It keeps track of your clients and their payments, sends invoices and reminders, and suspends or reactivates hosting automatically. It can set up accounts on hosting panels like cPanel, Plesk, and DirectAdmin and register domains with your registrar.

AutoBot AI lets you run an AI workspace on your own infrastructure with a knowledge base built from your documents and code. You can connect local or hosted models, build workflows visually, and add modules for things like transcription and codebase analysis. It also includes tools for managing the services across your machines. The Docker setup needs a language model before the chat can answer.

VeloxDB puts your databases in one desktop client so you don't need a different app for every connection. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis, and more. Write queries with table and column suggestions, browse results, or map out relationships in a visual diagram. It connects directly to your databases and stores credentials in your operating system's keychain.

Inkadra is a self-hosted workspace for filmmakers and photographers built with React on an infinite canvas. You can pin up mood boards, sketch storyboards, build shot lists, and plan shooting schedules, all drawing on the same data, so a change in one shows up in the others. Your team collaborates in real time with roles, comments, and notifications.

F1 Replay Timing is a web app for following Formula 1 sessions with live timing, car positions on a track map, and telemetry built with Next.js and Python on the FastF1 library. You can watch it live during a race weekend or replay any past session with full playback controls. It shows a driver leaderboard, race control messages, weather, and lap-by-lap analysis. And you can compare two drivers' telemetry side by side.

Sparrow is a self-hosted platform for sending webhooks to your customers, written in Go and shipped as a single binary that only needs PostgreSQL. Your services send it events and it delivers them to every subscriber, retrying with backoff until each one gets through. Every webhook is signed in the standard webhooks format so receivers can check it's really from you.

Sigwood is a command-line threat hunting tool for self-hosters that digs through the logs you already have. Point it at your Zeek, Pi-hole, Syslog, or AWS CloudTrail logs, and it runs 10 detectors looking for things like malware calling home on a schedule, strange DNS lookups, port scans, and unusual cloud activity. Every finding names the technique behind it, and it treats results as leads to check, not verdicts.

Keygate gives software developers a self-hosted way to manage licenses and subscriptions for their own products. You can set up trials, limit activations, track usage, and manage team seats from a dashboard. Connect Stripe and it can create a license when a customer pays. There's also a customer portal for managing activation slots, plus signed tokens for checking licenses offline.

Zeabur's open-source edition is a self-hosted platform for running apps on your own Kubernetes cluster or even a single machine, written in Rust. It reads what's already in your cluster and shows it as simple projects and services. Every action uses your own credentials and it keeps no database of its own. When something breaks, it explains the problem in plain language like a crash loop or an image that won't pull.

Templatical is a drag-and-drop email editor you can drop into your own app, built on Vue and rendering through MJML so emails look right in every inbox. It works inside React, Svelte, Angular, or plain JavaScript. You build an email from 14 block types or your own custom blocks which can even pull in live data from an API. Merge tags and show-or-hide conditions let one template fit each recipient.
